Editor's Word
Dr. Geofrey Okoboi
Ag. Director Corporate and Consumer Affairs
Welcome to the 20th issue of the Sector Update. This edition reflects the
Electricity Regulatory Authority's ongoing commitment to a reliable,
affordable, and inclusive electricity sector for all Ugandans.
This issue arrives at a pivotal moment as ERA stewards major transitions across the
electricity value chain. Our oversight remains squarely focused on protecting
consumer interests: ensuring continuity of service delivery, and safeguarding
quality and reliability as the transition unfolds. We will continue close monitoring
and proactive engagement to minimize disruption and uphold service standards.
Across the continent, the Africa Electricity Symposium shaped the dialogue on
energy policy, investment, and innovation. A key highlight from the Symposium
was the launch of the Youth Energy Summit, an important platform to deepen
youth engagement in the energy sector, nurture fresh talent, and catalyse home-
grown solutions to Africa's energy challenges.
Locally, ERA is expanding its footprint to improve regulatory oversight and service
quality: our new regional office in Mbarara city will strengthen monitoring and
responsiveness across the region. Complementing this expansion is our new
corporate strategy, which renews ERA's commitment to Electricity Supply Industry
(ESI) growth and efficiency, affordability of electricity, consumer protection, and
robust stakeholder engagement, all anchored on regulatory and institutional
excellence.
I invite you to explore this issue for in-depth coverage of these developments
and more. Thank you for your continued interest and partnership as we work to
secure a resilient, accessible, and sustainable energy future for Uganda.

ELECTRICITY TO SUPPORT THE
GOVERNMENT OF UGANDA’S TEN-
FOLD GROWTH AGENDA
Vianney Mutyaba
Manager Pricing
Uganda aspires to grow its Gross Domestic Product
(GDP) ten-fold, from USD 50 billion in 2023 to
USD 500 billion by 2040. To realize this ambition,
the Government of Uganda, through the Ministry of
Finance, Planning and Economic Development, has
formulated a Ten-Fold Growth Strategy anchored
on ATMS: Agro-Industrial Development, Tourism
Development, Mineral-Based Development, Oil & Gas,
and Multipliers (Science, Technology and Innovation,
ICT, and the Creative Industry).
Achievement of this ambition requires sustained
double-digit economic growth, which would position
Uganda among the most rapidly transformed
economies in recent history.
Electricity as a Critical Enabler of the Ten-Fold Growth
Strategy
The ATMS sectors, on their own, will not deliver the
ten-fold growth aspiration without the support of
critical enablers, foremost among them electricity.
Electricity plays a central and indispensable role in
underpinning Uganda’s ten-fold GDP growth agenda.
It is a prerequisite for rapid economic expansion
and a fundamental driver of structural economic
transformation.
The envisaged ten-fold GDP growth will be realized
largely through industrialization, particularly through
the establishment and expansion of industrial parks.
Industrialization, in turn, is heavily dependent on the
availability of electricity.

advancing Uganda’s electrification
and energy access programmes.
